provenance.source: NCERT Mathematics Class 8, Chapter 1 'Rational Numbers'. Definitions and standard form follow the textbook; the misconception list is not from the book — it is the set of errors that show up when Class 8 students are asked these questions, and each one is written so a distractor can point at it.
provenance.note: The mathematics here is self-checking and does not depend on which NCERT printing a school uses. The CHAPTER NUMBER does: NCERT is mid-transition under NCF-SE 2023 and the Class 8 book is being replaced. Confirm 'Rational Numbers' is still chapter 1 in the book your students hold before showing a chapter number in the UI.

concepts.title: What a rational number is
concepts.statement: Rational number wo number hai jise $\frac{p}{q}$ ke roop me likha ja sake, jahan $p$ aur $q$ dono integers hain aur $q \neq 0$. Har integer bhi rational hai, kyunki $5$ ko $\frac{5}{1}$ likha ja sakta hai.
concepts.hook: Socho ek pizza ke 8 barabar tukde hain aur tumne 3 khaye. Tumne $\frac{3}{8}$ pizza khaya. Ab socho tumne poora pizza khaya — wo $\frac{8}{8}$ yaani 1 hua. Aur agar tumne ek bhi tukda nahi khaya to $\frac{0}{8}$ yaani 0. Ye teeno — 3 tukde, poora, aur kuch nahi — teeno rational numbers hain. Sawal ye hai: kya pizza ko 0 tukdon me baanta ja sakta hai?

analogies.text: Rupee aur paise: 75 paise matlab $\frac{75}{100}$ rupaye. Har paisa ek rational number hai.
Cricket ka run rate: 240 run 50 over me matlab $\frac{240}{50}$ = 4.8 runs per over. Run rate hamesha ek rational number hota hai.

formulas.note: Ye definition hai. q ≠ 0 sabse important shart hai.
Isi wajah se har integer rational hai.

misconceptions.wrong_belief: Sirf fractions rational numbers hote hain. 7 jaisa poora number rational nahi hai.
misconceptions.why_wrong: Definition kehti hai ki number ko $\frac{p}{q}$ ke roop me likha ja SAKE — ye nahi ki wo pehle se fraction jaisa dikhe. 7 ko $\frac{7}{1}$ likha ja sakta hai, to 7 rational hai.
misconceptions.correction: Har integer rational hai. Denominator 1 laga do, ho gaya.
misconceptions.probe: 7 ko $\frac{p}{q}$ ke roop me likh sakte ho? Agar haan, to kya 7 rational hai?

misconceptions.wrong_belief: $\frac{5}{0}$ ka matlab 0 hota hai, ya bahut bada number hota hai.
misconceptions.why_wrong: $\frac{5}{0}$ ka koi matlab hi nahi hai. Bhaag ka matlab hai 'kitne barabar hisson me baanta' — 0 hisson me baantna ek kaam hi nahi hai. Isliye q ≠ 0 definition ka hissa hai, koi extra niyam nahi.
misconceptions.correction: Denominator kabhi 0 nahi. $\frac{5}{0}$ rational number hai hi nahi — wo undefined hai.
misconceptions.probe: $\frac{0}{5}$ aur $\frac{5}{0}$ — in dono me kaunsa rational number hai aur kaunsa hai hi nahi?

misconceptions.wrong_belief: Negative numbers rational nahi hote, kyunki hum unhe tukdon me nahi dekh sakte.
misconceptions.why_wrong: Definition me likha hai p aur q integers hain — aur integers me negative bhi aate hain. $-\frac{3}{4}$ me p = -3 hai, jo ek integer hai.
misconceptions.correction: $-\frac{3}{4}$ poori tarah rational hai. Negative hona koi rukawat nahi.
misconceptions.probe: $-\frac{3}{4}$ me p kya hai aur q kya hai? Dono integers hain kya?

misconceptions.wrong_belief: 0 rational number nahi hai kyunki wo 'kuch bhi nahi' hai.
misconceptions.why_wrong: 0 ko $\frac{0}{1}$ likha ja sakta hai — p = 0 ek integer hai, q = 1 ek integer hai aur 0 nahi hai. Dono shartein poori hain.
misconceptions.correction: 0 rational hai. Numerator 0 ho sakta hai; sirf denominator 0 nahi ho sakta.
misconceptions.probe: $\frac{0}{7}$ ka maan kya hai, aur kya wo rational number hai?

worked_examples.problem: Batao ki $-6$ ek rational number hai ya nahi. Kaaran ke saath.
steps: Rational hone ke liye number ko $\frac{p}{q}$ me likhna hoga, p aur q integers, q ≠ 0
Yahan p = -6 (integer hai) aur q = 1 (integer hai, aur 0 nahi hai)

worked_examples.problem: $\frac{0}{9}$ aur $\frac{9}{0}$ me se kaunsa rational number hai?
steps: $\frac{0}{9}$: yahan q = 9, jo 0 nahi hai. Shart poori — ye rational hai, aur iska maan 0 hai
$\frac{9}{0}$: yahan q = 0. Definition kehti hai q ≠ 0
Isliye $\frac{9}{0}$ rational number hai hi nahi — wo undefined hai

concepts.title: Standard form of a rational number
concepts.statement: Ek rational number standard form me tab hota hai jab uska denominator positive ho aur numerator-denominator me 1 ke alawa koi common factor na ho. Jaise $\frac{-12}{18}$ ka standard form $\frac{-2}{3}$ hai.
concepts.hook: Socho tum dukaan pe gaye aur 500 gram cheeni maangi. Dukaandar ne kaha 'aadha kilo'. Dono baat ek hi hai, par 'aadha kilo' bolna aasan hai. Standard form bhi yahi hai — same number, sabse saaf tareeke se likha hua. Sawal: $\frac{-12}{18}$ aur $\frac{12}{-18}$ — kya ye do alag numbers hain?

analogies.text: Address likhna: '3rd floor, flat 12' aur 'flat 12, 3rd floor' — ek hi ghar, par ek tareeka standard hai jise sab samajhte hain.
Score 6/10 aur 3/5 — ek hi performance, par 3/5 chhote numbers me likhi hui hai.

formulas.note: HCF se divide karne pe standard form aata hai.
Denominator ko positive banane ke liye upar-neeche dono ka sign badlo.

misconceptions.wrong_belief: Standard form matlab sirf denominator ko positive kar dena. HCF se divide karna zaroori nahi.
misconceptions.why_wrong: Standard form ki do shartein hain, ek nahi: denominator positive HO, aur numerator-denominator coprime HON. $\frac{-12}{18}$ ka denominator pehle se positive hai, phir bhi wo standard form me nahi hai.
misconceptions.correction: Do kaam karo — sign theek karo, phir HCF se divide karo. Dono ke bina standard form nahi.
misconceptions.probe: $\frac{-12}{18}$ ka denominator positive hai. Phir bhi ye standard form me kyun nahi hai?

misconceptions.wrong_belief: Standard form me numerator hamesha positive hona chahiye.
misconceptions.why_wrong: Shart denominator pe hai, numerator pe nahi. $\frac{-2}{3}$ poori tarah standard form me hai — denominator 3 positive hai aur 2 aur 3 coprime hain.
misconceptions.correction: Denominator positive hona chahiye. Numerator negative ho sakta hai.
misconceptions.probe: $\frac{-2}{3}$ standard form me hai ya nahi? Kaun si shart dekhni hai — numerator ya denominator?

misconceptions.wrong_belief: $\frac{2}{3}$ aur $\frac{4}{6}$ do alag rational numbers hain.
misconceptions.why_wrong: Dono ka maan bilkul ek hai — $\frac{4}{6}$ me upar-neeche dono ko 2 se divide karo to $\frac{2}{3}$ mil jaata hai. Alag likhawat, ek hi number.
misconceptions.correction: Equivalent rational numbers alag numbers nahi hain, ek hi number ke alag roop hain. Number line pe dono ek hi jagah baithte hain.
misconceptions.probe: $\frac{4}{6}$ ko upar-neeche 2 se divide karo. Kya mila? To kya ye $\frac{2}{3}$ se alag number hai?

misconceptions.wrong_belief: Standard form nikalne ke liye numerator aur denominator me se koi bhi common number se divide kar do — chhota ho jaaye bas.
misconceptions.why_wrong: Kisi bhi common factor se divide karne pe number chhota to ho jaata hai par standard form nahi aata. $\frac{12}{18}$ ko 2 se divide karke $\frac{6}{9}$ mila — 6 aur 9 me abhi bhi 3 common hai.
misconceptions.correction: HCF se divide karo, kisi bhi common factor se nahi. HCF ke baad kuch common bachta hi nahi.
misconceptions.probe: $\frac{12}{18}$ ko 2 se divide karne pe $\frac{6}{9}$ aaya. Kya ye standard form hai? 6 aur 9 me kuch common bacha hai kya?

steps: Denominator 18 pehle se positive hai, to sign wala kaam nahi karna
Upar aur neeche dono ko 6 se divide karo: $\frac{-12 \div 6}{18 \div 6} = \frac{-2}{3}$
Check: 2 aur 3 me 1 ke alawa kuch common nahi. Ho gaya
Denominator negative hai, to pehle upar-neeche dono ka sign badlo: $\frac{14}{-35} = \frac{-14}{35}$
Denominator 5 positive hai aur 2, 5 coprime hain

questions.stem: In me se kaunsa rational number NAHI hai?
questions.solution: Rational number ki shart hai $q \neq 0$. $\frac{7}{0}$ me denominator 0 hai, isliye wo rational number hai hi nahi — undefined hai. Baaki teeno rational hain: $\frac{0}{7} = 0$, $-7 = \frac{-7}{1}$, aur $\frac{-7}{2}$ pehle se $\frac{p}{q}$ roop me hai.

questions.stem: $5$ ko $\frac{p}{q}$ ke roop me kaise likhenge?

options.text: $5$ ko $\frac{p}{q}$ roop me likha hi nahi ja sakta

questions.solution: $5 = \frac{5}{1}$. Yahan p = 5 aur q = 1, dono integers hain aur q ≠ 0 — isliye 5 ek rational number hai.

questions.stem: $\frac{0}{9}$ ke baare me kaunsa kathan sahi hai?

options.text: Ye rational number hai aur iska maan 0 hai
Ye rational number nahi hai, kyunki 0 rational nahi hota
Ye rational hai par iska maan 9 hai

questions.solution: $\frac{0}{9}$ me denominator 9 hai, jo 0 nahi hai — to shart poori hai. Iska maan $0$ hai. Undefined tab hota jab denominator 0 hota, jaise $\frac{9}{0}$.

questions.stem: In me se kaun-kaun se rational numbers hain? (ek se zyada sahi ho sakte hain)
questions.solution: $-4 = \frac{-4}{1}$ rational hai, $\frac{0}{3} = 0$ rational hai, $\frac{-5}{8}$ rational hai. Sirf $\frac{3}{0}$ rational nahi hai kyunki denominator 0 hai.

questions.stem: Agar $\frac{p}{7}$ ek rational number hai aur uska maan $-2$ hai, to $p$ ka maan kya hoga?
Riya kehti hai: 'Har integer rational hai, par har rational integer nahi hai.' Ye kathan kaisa hai?

options.text: Sahi hai — $5 = \frac{5}{1}$ integer bhi hai aur rational bhi, par $\frac{1}{2}$ rational hai aur integer nahi
Galat hai — koi bhi integer rational nahi hota
Galat hai — har rational number integer hota hai
Sahi hai, par sirf positive numbers ke liye

questions.solution: Har integer $n$ ko $\frac{n}{1}$ likha ja sakta hai, to har integer rational hai. Ulta sach nahi: $\frac{1}{2}$ rational hai par integer nahi. Negative numbers is baat ko nahi badalte.

questions.stem: Samjhao ki $\frac{a}{0}$ kisi bhi $a$ ke liye rational number kyun nahi ho sakta, chahe $a$ kitna bhi bada ho.

rubric: Rational number ki definition batayi: $\frac{p}{q}$ jahan q ≠ 0
Bhaag ka matlab samjhaya — 0 barabar hisson me baantna ek kaam hi nahi hai
Ya: agar $\frac{a}{0} = x$ hota to $a = x \times 0 = 0$ hona chahiye, jo har a ke liye sach nahi
Nateeja: $\frac{a}{0}$ undefined hai, bada number nahi

questions.solution: Maan lo $\frac{a}{0} = x$. Bhaag ki definition se $a = x \times 0 = 0$. Yaani ye sirf tab ban sakta jab $a = 0$ ho, aur tab bhi $x$ koi bhi number ho sakta hai — ek hi jawab nahi milta. Isliye $\frac{a}{0}$ ka koi maan hai hi nahi. Ye 'bahut bada number' nahi hai, ye undefined hai.

options.text: $\frac{-12}{18}$ pehle se standard form me hai

questions.solution: HCF(12, 18) = 6. Upar-neeche dono ko 6 se divide karo: $\frac{-12 \div 6}{18 \div 6} = \frac{-2}{3}$. 2 se divide karne pe $\frac{-6}{9}$ milta hai, jisme abhi bhi 3 common hai — wo standard form nahi hai.

options.text: $\frac{4}{-9}$ pehle se standard form me hai

questions.solution: Standard form me denominator positive hona chahiye. Upar-neeche dono ka sign badlo: $\frac{4}{-9} = \frac{-4}{9}$. 4 aur 9 me 1 ke alawa kuch common nahi, to yahi standard form hai.

questions.stem: Kaunsa rational number $\frac{2}{3}$ ke barabar NAHI hai?
questions.solution: $\frac{4}{6}$, $\frac{-2}{-3}$ aur $\frac{10}{15}$ — teenon ka maan $\frac{2}{3}$ hai. $\frac{-4}{6}$ ka maan $\frac{-2}{3}$ hai, jo negative hai.

questions.stem: In me se kaunsa pehle se standard form me hai?
questions.solution: $\frac{-5}{7}$: denominator 7 positive hai aur HCF(5, 7) = 1. Dono shartein poori. $\frac{5}{-7}$ ka denominator negative hai; $\frac{10}{14}$ aur $\frac{-10}{14}$ me 2 common hai.

questions.stem: $\frac{-45}{60}$ ka standard form $\frac{p}{q}$ hai. $p + q$ ka maan kya hoga?
Arjun ne $\frac{24}{-36}$ ka standard form $\frac{-4}{6}$ nikala. Uski galti kya hai?

options.text: Usne 6 se divide kiya, par HCF 12 hai — 4 aur 6 me abhi bhi 2 common hai
Koi galti nahi, $\frac{-4}{6}$ hi sahi jawab hai
Usne sign galat kar diya, jawab $\frac{4}{6}$ hona chahiye
Usne ulta kar diya, jawab $\frac{-6}{4}$ hona chahiye

questions.solution: HCF(24, 36) = 12, 6 nahi. Sahi jawab $\frac{24}{-36} = \frac{-24}{36} = \frac{-2}{3}$ hai. Arjun ka sign sahi tha — galti sirf ye thi ki poora HCF nahi nikala.

questions.stem: Ek rational number ke anant (infinite) equivalent roop hote hain, par standard form sirf ek. Samjhao aisa kyun hai.

rubric: Equivalent roop banane ka tareeka: upar-neeche dono ko kisi bhi non-zero integer se guna karo
Aise integers anant hain, isliye equivalent roop anant hain
Standard form ki do shartein: denominator positive, aur HCF = 1
In dono shartein ek saath sirf ek hi jodi (p, q) pe poori hoti hain, isliye standard form unique hai

questions.solution: $\frac{2}{3}$ ko $\frac{4}{6}, \frac{6}{9}, \frac{8}{12}, \dots$ likha ja sakta hai — upar-neeche dono ko kisi bhi non-zero integer se guna karke. Aise guna karne wale integers anant hain, to roop bhi anant. Par jab hum kehte hain ki denominator positive ho AUR HCF 1 ho, to har baar ek hi jodi bachti hai — is case me (2, 3). Isiliye standard form unique hota hai aur do numbers ko compare karne ka bharosemand tareeka hai.
